title: Automatic Design for Modular Microfluidic Routing Blocks
problem: Designing microfluidic routing blocks that interconnect pumps, cell cultures, and other modules is a cumbersome, repetitive, manual task, hindering rapid development of organs-on-chip devices.
motivation: Recent ISO standardization of modular microfluidic building blocks enables reusable components, but manual routing design remains a bottleneck for implementing organ-on-chip systems.
method: Proposes an automated design and routing method that fully automates interconnection of microfluidic chip components. Provides user-friendly interactive online tool as part of Munich Microfluidic Toolkit (MMFT).
key_novelty: Automated routing method for modular microfluidic systems following ISO standardization.
contributions: Automated design method for microfluidic routing blocks
Automated interconnection of pumps, cell cultures, and module components
User-friendly interactive online tool in MMFT
Feasibility demonstrated on physically fabricated routing blocks

metrics.other: Significant reduction in design effort and time

limitations: Evaluation on organ-on-chip applications only; applicability to other microfluidic systems not explored.
